## Summary
- add `pi` to provider resolution, model policy, workflow setup, and runtime installation
- restore `PI_AUTH_JSON_B64` / `PI_AUTH_JSON` only for Pi runs with isolated auth and cleanup
- keep Pi session setup conservative and bundle Pi session logs without auth secrets
- update onboarding and docs for Pi configuration and OAuth refresh-token caveats

## Tests
- `npm test`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #350

## Notes

- The strongest rubric fit is the revised design direction: this PR uses existing ACPX provider plumbing and adds Pi at the resolver/setup/session/auth boundaries instead of creating a parallel adapter.
- Conservative Pi session setup is handled explicitly: Pi receives configured model setup but returns before Codex `thought_level` and `set-mode full-access` commands. Evidence: [acpx-adapter.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/d580b974ff3d5507f1fb7bd7956c38e7c211e126/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L297-L319), [acpx-adapter.test.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/d580b974ff3d5507f1fb7bd7956c38e7c211e126/.agent/src/__tests__/acpx-adapter.test.ts#L495-L510).
- Regression coverage is focused on the requested surfaces: resolver auto/override behavior, Pi auth restoration, conservative setup, workflow wiring, onboarding, and session bundles.
- No rubric-specific follow-up needed.

## Findings

- **INFO:** No blocking or warning-level rubric findings. The implementation satisfies the applicable selected rubrics with only small documentation-density and auth-glue complexity trade-offs.

## Final Rubric Verdict

PASS
